highlights.title: Fix alarm sounds and Low-Soon alerts
changes: Device alarms now use your selected tone and Play Sound setting when they fire.
Alarm sound files are bundled so system notifications can resolve and play chosen tones.
Delayed critical alarms now start their audio when they actually fire instead of remaining silent.
Low Glucose Soon alerts are evaluated and will fire even when a CGM app handles reading-driven alerts.
On iOS 26+, Trio will use AlarmKit so critical alarms can ring when the app is suspended and pierce Silent/Focus.

Use AlarmKit for critical alarms on iOS 26+

includedPullRequests.title: Fix Alarm  Sounds and Low-Soon Alerts; add AlarmKit for >= iOS 26
includedPullRequests.body:
Alarm sounds never reached the user. Four independent causes, one per commit.

Fixes #1371
Fixes #1428

### Causes

1. Device Alarms config (tone, Play Sound, Override Silence & Focus, day/night window) stopped being applied to catalog-known alerts in `00bdcb84b`; only the interruption level survived the switch to catalog routing. Plugins issue alerts with `sound: nil`, so device alarms had no tone at all.
2. Tones shipped as an Xcode folder reference, so they built to `Trio.app/Sounds/`. `UNNotificationSound(named:)` resolves only against the bundle root and `Library/Sounds`, so iOS silently substituted the default sound. The picker preview and `CriticalAlertAudioPlayer` worked because they were the only paths passing `subdirectory: "Sounds"`.
3. The critical-audio fallback, which is what pierces the silent switch and Focus without the Critical Alerts entitlement, rejected anything not `.immediate`. The not-looping watchdog is the only `.delayed` alert Trio creates, so the one alarm that fires unattended never got audio.
4. `evaluateForecast` bailed on the same CGM-ownership guard as the reading path, so Low Glucose Soon was never evaluated on Dexcom, xDrip4iOS or Libre, where "Use CGM App Alerts" defaults on.

### Commits

| Commit | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `86061e0` | Register the 18 `.caf` files individually so they flatten to the bundle root; drop the now-wrong `subdirectory:` from both lookups. Vendor sounds move to a flat `Library/Sounds/<manager>-<file>`. |
| `1420ca6` | Start playback from the modal scheduler's timer, whose `.insert` decision already means live, not stale, not snoozed. `.immediate` still plays at issue time. |
| `22dbce0` | Drop the CGM-ownership guard from `evaluateForecast`. A CGM app cannot compute Trio's oref forecast, so it can never cover this alarm. `evaluateCarbsRequired` already omits it, and the settings screen only moves reading-driven types into "Handled by CGM App". |
| `cdc46d2` | AlarmKit for critical alarms on iOS 26+, ported from Loop's `CriticalAlertAlarmScheduler`. Needs no entitlement and still fires when iOS has suspended Trio. Plays the user's selected tone. Stop acknowledges the alert rather than only silencing it. |

Earlier commit `690f24f0` (opt-in Critical Alerts entitlement) was dropped from this branch.

### Coverage

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Critical, immediate, app running | default iOS sound | selected tone, pierces silent + Focus |
| Critical, delayed (not-looping) | silent | selected tone at fire time |
| Critical, app suspended, iOS 26+ | not possible | AlarmKit, selected tone |
| Critical, app suspended, iOS 17-25 | not possible | still not possible without the entitlement |

### Testing

Full suite green, 565 tests / 82 suites. New tests assert every `AlarmSoundCatalog` filename resolves via `Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:)`, the call shape iOS uses, so a folder reference cannot silently regress this again.

Not covered by tests, needs a device: tone actually playing, piercing Silent and Focus, AlarmKit ringing on a suspended app, Stop acknowledging the alert. The AlarmKit custom tone in particular is unverified here.
